analysis.title: Who Pulled The Plug On Power Up America
key_insights: The AI power-demand trade has sold off hard even though the demand story is unchanged. Hedge funds have cut exposure since May and positioning is at multi-year lows.
Hedge fund long/short positioning in the Power Up America theme is in the 3rd percentile since 2020 (MS PB data).
Goldman PB data shows positioning in both the broader Power Up America basket and grid infrastructure near two-year lows. Nuclear names have also been sold.
Valuations of the IPPs and GEV (GSXUIPPS) are near a 2-year low.

Goldman hosted 400+ clients on short notice and said it likes buying the Power Up America basket, calling it the most underappreciated AI bottleneck. It says positioning is low, valuation has normalized and fundamentals are intact.
Of the theme's 5 categories, all but Grid Infrastructure underperformed the S&P 500 excluding AI.
Goldman expects US data center electricity demand to rise from 39 GW in 2025 to 108 GW by 2030, a 23% CAGR. It expects total US power demand to grow 3.5% a year through 2030.

Constellation announced PPAs with Google for about 3.6 GW of nuclear in PJM, following a 20-year ~700 MW nuclear PPA with Amazon the prior week. Goldman expects higher earnings revisions as IPPs sign long-term deals with mega-cap tech.
Morgan Stanley expects contracting activity to accelerate in 2027 and sees an 'extremely attractive' entry point for the group. It says IPPs trade at levels implying no further contracting upside.
